text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure is often called a "silent killer" because it usually causes no warning signs or symptoms at all.
snippet_highlighted_words: no warning signs or symptoms at all

list.snippet: No physical clues: Most people with high blood pressure feel completely fine and do not know they have it.
Only way to know: Measuring your blood pressure with a cuff is the only reliable way to find out if your numbers are high. You can learn more from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text_blocks.snippet: When blood pressure is very high or spikes suddenly, some people may notice mild or easy-to-miss signs:

list.snippet: Early-morning headaches (a dull ache when waking up)
Blood spots in the eyes or occasional nosebleeds

text_blocks.snippet: If your blood pressure reading is higher than 180/120 mm Hg, it is a medical emergency. Call 911 immediately if you have extreme high blood pressure along with any of these danger signs:

list.snippet: Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
Numbness, weakness, or trouble speaking (signs of a stroke)

text_blocks.snippet: Read more about warning signs and risks on the American Heart Association or detailed mechanisms on the Cleveland Clinic.
If you'd like, let me know:

list.snippet: Your recent blood pressure readings if you have them
Whether you are currently feeling any specific symptoms

text_blocks.snippet: I can help you understand what those numbers mean or when to seek care.
